tieu_de: Annual profections: the 2,000-year-old technique for knowing what your year is about
mo: The arithmetic: one house per year
Where the lord sits in your natal chart
Transits to the lord: when things get real
Why it needs whole sign houses

There's a timing technique older than transits, simple enough to do in your head, and still the first thing Hellenistic astrologers check when they look at a year. It's called annual profections. Each year of your life activates one house of your chart, and the planet ruling that house becomes the lord of the year.
This guide covers the arithmetic, the age table, the lord of the year and what to do with it, how profections filter transits, the monthly version, and why it requires whole sign houses.

muc.ten: The arithmetic: one house per year
doan: Your first year of life (birth to first birthday) belongs to the 1st house. The second year, the 2nd house. And so on through the 12th, then back to the 1st at age 12. The 12-year cycle repeats for life.
Formula: take your age (completed birthdays), divide by 12, take the remainder, add 1. That's the house of the year.
Age 18, 30, 42, 54: 7th house
Age 21, 33, 45, 57: 10th house
Age 29, 41, 53: 6th house
You can do this for yourself right now. That's the appeal.
Planet Saturn Rules Capricorn Discipline, responsibility, structure
Planet Sun Rules Leo Ego, will, vitality
House House 7 Marriage, business partners, open enemies, contracts, cooperation
A few landmarks from the table:

Age 29 is a 6th-house year (work, health, service) and 30 is a 7th-house year (partnership, marriage). It's no accident that so many people change jobs at 29 and get married at 30. The Saturn return lands in the same window, so the two techniques reinforce each other.
Ages 24 and 36 return to the 1st house: reinvention years, often a change of appearance or direction.
Ages 27, 39, 51 are 4th-house years: home, parents, roots, moving.
Ages 35, 47, 59 are 12th-house years: a year of withdrawal, endings, tiredness with no obvious cause. Not bad, but not a launch year.
Ages 21, 33, 45 are 10th-house years: career and public visibility.
The house gives the theme. But the theme is only half. The other half is the lord.

Each house begins with a sign, and each sign has a ruler in the traditional scheme (Aries and Scorpio: Mars; Taurus and Libra: Venus; Gemini and Virgo: Mercury; Cancer: Moon; Leo: Sun; Sagittarius and Pisces: Jupiter; Capricorn and Aquarius: Saturn). The ruler of the sign on the profected house is the lord of the year.

Example: you're 30, so it's a 7th-house year. Your 7th house is Capricorn. The lord of the year is Saturn. Every partnership matter that year goes through a Saturn filter: slow, serious, commitment or ending, nothing half-hearted.
Same age, but your 7th house is Leo: the lord is the Sun. A partnership year, but in the mode of being seen, being acknowledged, the year of the public wedding or of introducing someone to everyone.
The lord of the year is the planet to watch for those 12 months. Every transit to it lands harder than usual.

muc.ten: Where the lord sits in your natal chart
doan: Next step: find the lord of the year in your birth chart. Its sign, house, and aspects tell you where the year's theme gets worked out.

Continuing the example: the lord is Saturn, and your natal Saturn sits in the 10th house. The 7th-house year (partnership) will be lived through the 10th (career): a business partnership, a partner met through work, or a marriage that affects your public standing.

If the lord is well placed natally (in a sign it likes, with supportive aspects), the year runs smoother whatever the theme. If it's poorly placed (in a sign it struggles in, squared by something hard), the year asks more effort.

muc.ten: Transits to the lord: when things get real
doan: This is where profections and transits meet, and why profections come first.

In any year there are dozens of transits. You can't track them all. Profections give you a filter: transits to the lord of the year, or through the profected house, are the ones to watch. Other transits still happen, but they tend to be quieter.

Example: 7th-house year, lord Venus. If transiting Jupiter conjoins your natal Venus that year, that's the clearest moment of the year's relationship theme. The same Jupiter transit in a year when Venus isn't the lord is just a pleasant week.
Profections answer "what." Transits answer "when."

The technique has a monthly version: starting from the profected house at your birthday, advance one house per month. The first month after your birthday is the house of the year; the second month is the next house; and after 12 months you're back at the next birthday.

This gives a smaller rhythm inside the yearly one. The month whose profected house coincides with a house full of natal planets tends to be busy. The month whose lord is being transited hard is one to save your strength for.

muc.ten: Why it needs whole sign houses
doan: Profections are Hellenistic, and they were built on whole sign houses: each sign is one house, and the rising sign is the whole 1st house. With whole signs, every house starts at 0 degrees of a sign, so the lord of the year is always unambiguous.

Using a quadrant system (Placidus, Koch) with profections produces a mess, because house cusps fall mid-sign and some signs get intercepted. Astrolas calculates profections in whole signs regardless of the house system you use for your natal chart, to keep the technique intact. If you want to understand where the two systems differ, there's a separate guide to whole sign versus Placidus.

Open the annual profections tool with your birth date, time, and place. It gives the house of the year, the lord of the year, where the lord sits natally, the monthly table, and the transits currently touching the lord.

A good test: pick your age-30 year (if you've had it) or any year you remember well. Look at the lord of that year and its natal house, then recall what the year was about. For most people this is the first time they see a technique this simple match this closely.

Profections don't replace transits or solar returns. They're the first step: know which house this year lights up and which planet holds the key, then open the more detailed tools to see when the key turns.
